title: Klara and the Sun
pitch: A Nobel laureate's quiet novel told by Klara, an Artificial Friend bought to keep a sick girl company, who watches people with love and misunderstanding.

chapters.g: Klara waits in a shop window, learning about people by watching the street and believing the Sun gives nourishment.
Klara comes to live with Josie, a girl who is ill, and her worried mother.
A world where some children are genetically lifted, with costs no one talks about.
Klara learns why she was really chosen, and what Josie's mother hopes she might become.
Klara makes a private sacrifice to try to save Josie.
What happens to an Artificial Friend when she is no longer needed.

ideas: An AI can be deeply caring and still misread the world.
People may try to replace those they love.
What makes a person unique is hard to copy.
How we treat helpers we no longer need says a lot about us.

args.a: Klara shows that an AI could have real devotion.
args.c: Readers disagree whether Klara feels or only imitates, and the book leaves it open.

args.a: A person cannot simply be continued in a machine.
args.c: The novel suggests uniqueness lives in others' love, not in data, which some find too hopeful.

questions: What do we owe a helper AI at the end of its use?
Could you be learned and copied?

quiz.q: What does Klara believe gives nourishment?
quiz.w: She runs on solar power and builds a faith around it.
